audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Gnar / Skill / Yone / Yone / Gnar / Yone / Yone while the already-audited mirror settled on Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Yone, and whys[1] and whys[2] here both describe Gnar winning those levels while the enum said Skill and Yone.
audit.why: Mini Gnar out-ranges Mortal Steel's 450 units with a 1100-range Boomerang Throw and Hyper autos, so the first two levels are his; from level 3 the lane is a Rage-bar read rather than a fixed winner, and you only take it outright once he is a Mini target with two items.
audit.corrected: Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Yone — the swing is the Rage bar, not the level.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treated level 6 as Gnar's spike and told you to track GNAR! on a cooldown.
audit.why: GNAR! only exists in Mega form, so it is gated by the Rage bar rather than a clock — the listed 90/60/30s only starts once he has transformed. Hop is 22s at rank 1 down to 12s; Wallop is 7s; Boomerang Throw is 16s at rank 1 and refunds on catch. Your own spikes are Soul Unbound falling 22s to 10s and the first crit item.
audit.corrected: Read the Rage bar for his spike; yours are Soul Unbound's shrinking cooldown, first item, and every Mini window in between.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed described as setting up 'team knockups nothing can dodge'; the GNAR! wall-stun condition never stated in the don'ts.
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward Yone — Riot's text has no airborne and the kit carries no knockup flag on his R. GNAR! only stuns enemies it throws into a wall, so terrain, not the ability, decides whether it locks you down. Mortal Steel's second stack is your own airborne and it ignores tenacity.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed pulls rather than knocks up. Fight Mega in open ground — with no wall behind you, GNAR! is a knockback and slow instead of a stun.

edits.before: Level 3 Gnar can Hop to kite your E dash and still out-trade you.
edits.after: Level 3 evens out: Hop is 22s at rank 1, so his kite has real gaps.

edits.before: Your first item gives you the burst to punish Mini Gnar windows and flip the lane.
edits.after: Your first item buys burst to punish Mini windows, but a Mega bar resets it.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gnar's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last enemy and pulls; it never knocks up. GNAR! only exists in Mega, so read his Rage bar, not the clock.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Gnar carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed pulls the enemies it clips toward you instead of knocking them up. Gnar carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. Fight mini form. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Watch the Rage bar, not a timer — Mega is the all-in, so fight him while Mini.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Fight mini form. When it is down — Q3-R him.
edits.after: GNAR! exists only in Mega, so read the Rage bar. Mini's Hop is 22s at rank 1 — punish inside it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Mega's GNAR! stuns you against a wall — never fight it near terrain.

notes: Five chart rows flipped in matched pairs onto the mirror's chart, which the packet also supports for the early rows; whys[2] and whys[5] were rewritten so the prose no longer contradicts the enum it sits next to. The key mechanical correction is that GNAR! is Rage-gated rather than cooldown-gated, so the templated 'engage only on GNAR!'s cooldown' phrasing in loading, breakdown.mid and report[9] is wrong in kind — I fixed the two highest-traffic instances but focus.text would have to change for the rest to read coherently. Also stated: the GNAR! stun only lands if you are thrown into a wall.
